title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: bring your own detections as custom indicators
summary: Hold: the policy configuration route omits choices that determine the wizard's next pages, including the policy category and content-priority branch. The roadmap facts, preview behaviour, default state, licensing qualification and documented limits are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans customer-supplied activity indicators from homegrown, SIEM/UEBA and line-of-business systems for existing Insider Risk Management playbooks.
claims.quote:
Allow customers to bring their own user activity
indicators from homegrown, SIEM/UEBA platforms, or other line-of-business
applications, and leverage them in existing Insider Risk Management playbooks.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes the Insider Risk Indicators connector as preview.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The capability imports preprocessed, aggregated SIEM detections.
claims.quote: To bring your own detections to the insider risk management solution, import preprocessed, aggregated detections from security information and event management (SIEM) solutions such as Microsoft Sentinel or Splunk.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Raw detection signals cannot be imported; the supported input is preprocessed aggregations as a file.
claims.quote: Currently, you can't import "raw" detection signals into insider risk management. You can only import preprocessed aggregations as a file.

claims.claim: The Insider Risk Indicators connector must exist before a custom indicator is created.
claims.quote: To create a custom indicator to import third-party indicator data, you must first create an Insider Risk Indicators connector (preview).

claims.claim: The sample script uploads CSV data rather than configuring the connector or policy.
claims.quote: The last step in setting up a connector is running a sample script that uploads the data in the CSV file. When you run the script, the connector you created in Step 3 imports the data to your Microsoft 365 organization

claims.claim: Custom indicators can only be used with Data theft and Data leaks templates.
claims.quote: You can only use custom indicators with the Data theft and Data leaks templates.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Crossing the configured trigger threshold can bring a user into policy scope.
claims.quote: When user activity crosses the threshold value that you specify for the policy, the user is brought into scope of the insider risk management policy

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The user brought into scope is scored for risk.
claims.quote: the user is brought into scope of the insider risk management policy and is scored for risk.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Learn describes an alert that analysts can investigate using custom indicator details.
claims.quote: An alert is generated and analysts can investigate the alert using custom indicator details.

claims.claim: A homegrown leaver-prediction model is a documented example of a custom trigger.
claims.quote: This example shows how to structure a CSV file to create a 'home-grown' trigger that could be used to predict the probability of an employee leaving an organization.

claims.claim: Salesforce and Dropbox activities can be supplied as custom indicators alongside built-in detections.
claims.quote: you might want to extend your detections to include Salesforce and Dropbox activities and use them alongside the built-in detections provided by insider risk management

claims.claim: Identified insider risks can lead to investigation cases.
claims.quote: After identifying the risks, you can take action to mitigate these risks, and if necessary open investigation cases and take appropriate legal action.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: The documented preview is admin-opt-in because an administrator must configure the connector, indicators and policy before it operates.
claims.quote:
Bringing your own detections to insider risk management is a three-step process:
1. In Microsoft Purview, create the Insider Risk Indicators (preview) connector as described in this article.

claims.claim: All global indicators are disabled by default.
claims.quote: All global indicators are disabled by default; you must select one or more indicators to configure an Insider Risk Management policy.

claims.claim: Each imported record must identify the user by UserPrincipalName.
claims.quote: Only the UserPrincipalName and date/time fields are mandatory.

claims.claim: Each imported record must contain an event time.
claims.quote: Mandatory field that displays the date/time that the activity occurred.

claims.claim: Optional imported fields appear in Activity explorer, alerts and cases.
claims.quote: All other fields are optional but can be helpful for the analyst or investigator in decision making when they triage alerts (these fields appear in the Activity explorer and in alerts and cases).

claims.claim: The sample script uploads the supplied data to the Microsoft cloud.
claims.quote: The sample script that you run in Step 4 uploads your data to the Microsoft cloud so that the insider risk management solution can use it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A registered Microsoft Entra application authenticates the connector and upload script.
claims.quote: When you create this app, Microsoft Entra ID can authenticate the connector when it runs and attempts to access your organization. Use this app to authenticate the script that you run in Step 4 to upload your data to the Microsoft cloud.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance

claims.quote: .\HRConnector.ps1 -tenantId "aaaabbbb-0000-cccc-1111-dddd2222eeee" -appId "00001111-aaaa-2222-bbbb-3333cccc4444" -appSecret "Aa1Bb~2Cc3.-Dd4Ee5Ff6Gg7Hh8Ii9_Jj0Kk1Ll2"

claims.claim: The sample script is not supported under a Microsoft standard support program.
claims.quote: This sample script isn't supported under any Microsoft standard support program or service.

claims.claim: The webhook.ingestion.office.com domain must be allowed through the firewall for the script to run.
claims.quote: Make sure to add the webhook.ingestion.office.com domain to your firewall allowlist for your organization. If this domain is blocked, the script doesn't run.

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to set a custom threshold rather than use default thresholds for a selected custom trigger or indicator.
claims.quote: After selecting your custom trigger or indicator, make sure to set a custom threshold (don't use the default thresholds).

claims.claim: Trigger thresholds cannot be set when Use only as a triggering event without any thresholds is selected.
claims.quote: You can't set trigger thresholds on a custom indicator if you select the Use only as a triggering event without any thresholds option.

claims.claim: A record sharing a timestamp and UPN with another record in the uploaded file is dropped.
claims.quote: If any record in the uploaded CSV file contains the same timestamp and UPN as other records in the file, the record is dropped.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft says to wait 24 hours after updating custom indicators and associated policies before uploading data to avoid unscored data during synchronization.
claims.quote: Make sure to wait 24 hours before uploading the data after you update the custom indicators and the associated policies. This waiting period ensures all components sync.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Insider Risk Management requires a supported subscription and appropriate licences assigned to users, supporting the per-user model.
claims.quote: To access and use Insider Risk Management, administrators need to verify their organization has a supported subscription and assign the appropriate licenses to users.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licence requirement specific to custom indicators or the Insider Risk Indicators connector is not published separately.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management custom indicators import connector licensing pricing pay as you go; "insider risk" "custom indicators" "license". Read Get started licensing, import-insider-risk-indicators, policy indicators and Purview billing models; no separate requirement stated.

claims.claim: The billing page meters the listed cloud storage, cloud service and Fabric indicators in data security processing units.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management indicators that detect activity in cloud storage apps (Box, Dropbox, Google Drive), cloud services (AWS, Azure), and Microsoft Fabric (Power BI) are billed on data security processing units.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The billing documentation does not identify a meter or charge specifically for imported custom indicators.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management custom indicators import connector licensing pricing pay as you go. Read purview-billing-models, policy indicators and connector documentation; the billed categories are cloud and generative AI indicators, with no custom-indicator charge specified.

claims.claim: Microsoft suggests scheduling the upload script to run daily.
claims.quote: After you run the script, consider scheduling a task to run it automatically on a daily basis so the most current data is uploaded to the Microsoft cloud.

claims.claim: The CSV data needs updating on a schedule similar to the upload schedule.
claims.quote: This schedule requires updating the data in the CSV file on a similar (if not the same) schedule so that it contains the latest information.

claims.claim: Learn describes Insider Risk Management availability in tenants hosted in regions and countries supported by Azure service dependencies.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management is currently available in tenants hosted in geographical regions and countries supported by Azure service dependencies.

claims.claim: Creating the connector requires the Data Connector Admin role.
claims.quote: Assign the Data Connector Admin role to the user who creates the connector in Step 3. This role is required to add connectors on the Data connectors page in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Both the Insider Risk Management and Insider Risk Management Admins role groups can configure policies and settings.
claims.quote:
| Actions | Insider Risk Management | Insider Risk Management Admins |
| Configure policies and settings | Yes | Yes |

claims.claim: Multiple role groups include the Data Connector Admin role by default.
claims.quote: Multiple role groups include this role by default.

claims.claim: Role-group membership is configured in the Purview portal at Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote:
Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page, select Roles and groups, then select Roles groups in the left navigation pane.
Select the Insider Risk Management role group, then select Edit.
Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember with Identity "Insider Risk Management" and Member set to a user UPN adds that user to the role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The connector creation entry point is Purview portal > Settings > Data connectors > My connectors > Add connector > Insider Risk Indicators (preview).
claims.quote:
Select Settings > Data connectors.
Select My connectors, then select Add connector.
From the list, select Insider Risk Indicators (preview).

claims.claim: Custom indicator creation is reached through Insider Risk Management > Settings > Policy indicators > Custom Indicators > Add custom indicator.
claims.quote:
In Insider Risk Management settings, select Policy indicators and then select the Custom Indicators tab.
Select Add custom indicator.

claims.claim: Only a Number field can supply a custom indicator threshold value.
claims.quote: Only fields that have a Number data type appear in the Data from mapping file list, since a Number data type is required to set a threshold value. The data type is specified when you set up the connector.

claims.claim: Custom indicator insights appear in alerts, Activity explorer and the User timeline.
claims.quote: After adding the custom indicator to your policies, the triggers and insights generated based on the custom indicators appear in the Alerts dashboard, Activity explorer, and User timeline.

claims.claim: Connector configuration maps the event time and Microsoft 365 user email address fields.
claims.quote: Enter the values for Event time (UTC time) and Microsoft 365 user email address based on the appropriate values from the CSV file. These fields are mandatory for the connector.

claims.claim: A custom indicator is created before it is added to a policy.
claims.quote:
Select Add indicator. The indicator is added to the Custom Indicators list.
Now you can add the custom indicator to an insider risk policy
